summary: Scheduled 60-second public-information probes consumed the deployed release's default 1000/day quotas for the root and metadata endpoints, making quota exhaustion visible to traffic sharing an exhausted application-visible identity.
impact: The public landing page and metadata endpoint returned HTTP 429 to affected traffic, while the relay remained healthy and health, version, and compute polling requests continued succeeding in retained evidence.
fix: Status is operationally Resolved as of 2026-09-05T19:53:19Z. Production Helm revision 7 runs ghcr.io/futuroptimist/tokenplace-relay:sha-6c39adc (OCI index sha256:543fde33aff45253630090b52d16163e3586da12c973f5c4a658ddc8927d0a68; source 6c39adc64e7bed4f85d07164aa2860e637919ca9; public version 0.1.1). Root and metadata probes were restored alongside the continuously active health probes; each restored target had three successful samples with min_over_time(probe_success)=1. Authenticated application scraping was also restored. During final verification compute polls rose from 222 to 260, memory stayed between 65,101,824 and 65,425,408 bytes of 268,435,456, and restarts, HTTP 429, and HTTP 5xx remained zero. No intentionally disabled monitoring functionality remains.
lessons: Release parity must preserve reviewed safety fixes; synthetic request frequency must be validated against endpoint quotas, quota pressure needs privacy-safe early warning, and process replacement is a risky reset rather than a permanent correction. Operational resolution is separate from preventive-work completion, so all linked action-item issues remain open pending independent implementation and verification.
